_comment: DECLARED RULING/CODE PAIRS. A ruling document says what the estate does; a script does it. This
registry names the pairs so ops\audit-ruling-drift.ps1 can check that the code still agrees with
the document, which nothing did before 2026-09-06 (backlog E12).
ops\audit-twin-drift.ps1 covers CODE-to-CODE duplication - one rule implemented in two files. This
covers DOCUMENT-to-CODE: a ruling that changes without a deploy, and a script that does not notice.
Different failure, different registry, deliberately not merged.
EVERY ENTRY IS A DECISION SOMEONE DEFENDS IN A DIFF. `absent` means the symbol must NOT appear in
the file; `present` means it must. `why` is not decoration - an entry whose reason nobody can state
is an entry nobody can retire.

rulings.ruled: Brad, 2026-09-04: remove ALL hardcoded bands. The bands are specified per-run and could fluctuate, so should never be hard coded.
rulings.why: Section 3.3 of the brief: delete DEFAULT_COND once nothing reads them - a constant that exists is a constant something will use. It still states 350-650 cal in PROSE and resolve_conditions still falls back to it, so a run that states no conditions tells its machine gate one band and every agent a different one, silently. That exact defect already fired on hunt-2026-08-27-ten.
Section 3.2: `self.band = dict(band or DEFAULT_BAND)` must become a refusal. A band nobody typed is a band nobody agreed to, and two gates would enforce it silently for a whole run.
Section 3.3 names the harvest.py trio. A hard-coded 650 here once buried 1,556 candidates - 64% of the pool - against a band nobody had stated for that run.

rulings.ruled: Brad's ruling 1, 2026-09-07: pork and beans is NOT a baked bean. The include pattern admitted it while known-wrong.json ruled the same product wrong at Hy-Vee, so the rule and the ledger disagreed at two other stores.
rulings.why: Measured on the 2026-09-07 board: six baked-beans cells, four true baked beans and two pork-and-beans, with the CROWN on 'Fareway Pork and Beans' at 0.0593 - so the cheapest cell was a different product from the four it was compared against. Re-adding this pattern hands the crown back to an adjacent cheaper product; that is the commodity-hijack shape the 2026-08-08 Hy-Vee ruling names.

rulings.ruled: Brad's ruling 4, 2026-09-07: leave the band-censorship median discriminator at 0.4, not 0.3.
rulings.why: 0.3 keeps four arguable rows but leaves the 1/16 deli row (0.318) standing, and a ratchet with a known false positive in it is one people learn to scroll past. The cost of 0.4 is recorded rather than hidden: the rows the floor retires are counted and named on every run (14 on 2026-09-07). Changing this number without changing that report would make the trade invisible again.

rulings.ruled: Brad's ruling 7, 2026-09-07: keep the commodity-level kind_equivalent declaration rather than reverting to per-size allowlist entries.
rulings.why: A physics fact about a commodity is re-derivable; a per-size allowlist entry is a decision nobody can re-derive, which is the failure the retire_when discipline exists for (2026-07-30: two entries justified by 'the store does not carry the item' while the store carried it). Per-size entries are also unbounded - a new size needs a new review, and every review is a chance to be wrong. Removing the declaration silently restores that review queue.

rulings.ruled: Brad's ruling 2, 2026-09-07: allowlist the memory store's private backup remote, and make the guard PROVE it private on every run rather than forbidding all remotes.
rulings.why: The allowlist alone would be strictly WEAKER than the rule it replaced - it would let a repository be flipped to public without anything noticing, because nothing would ever look. The probe is the half that makes the ruling safe, and an allowlist entry with no live probe behind it is exactly the reviewed-exception-that-stopped-being-checked shape. If this symbol goes, ops/memory-remote-allowlist.json must go with it.
